claim: P5 algorithm-vs-stack ratio ROBUSTNESS audit on iter-193 headline (60.6x reward, 10.3x zvf, 4.8x len). 4 paired-bootstrap stress tests (B=2000, seed 20260706, 95% CI) on 15 (ch x stack axis) cells: paired-bootstrap CI on the ratio excludes 1.0 on zvf AND reward for at least one axis (H1 PASS); excludes 3.0 (H2 PASS); the DOMINANT axes (model_family / task_slice / G) each individually carry the signal (H3 PASS); NOISY axes (seed / temperature) DO NOT exclude 1.0 on any channel because their eta^2 is approx 0 (H4 PASS scope-clarification). Drop a dominant axis -> OTHER dominant axes still exclude 1.0 (H5' PASS): drop task_slice -> G still excludes 1; drop model_family -> task_slice still excludes 1 on reward; drop G -> task_slice still excludes 1 on zvf. Signal propagates, not a single-axis artifact. Naive jackknife over ALL axes (H5 FAIL): once you remove the dominant axis, the worst remaining is seed/temperature and comparison degenerates. Naive 5-axis composite (additive main-effects, Cohen 1973 / Hays 1973) gives eta^2_composite = 0.0441 (zvf), 0.0316 (reward); ratio CI includes 1.0 for both (H6 FAIL): averaging noisy axes dilutes signal below detection. Even 3-dominant-axis composite gives eta^2 = 0.1211 (zvf, 2.67x), 0.0877 (reward, 11.75x); zvf still fails because dominant axes are correlated. Sharp reading: iter-193 headline is NOT a single-axis cherry-pick (H5' PASS) but is axis-conditional (H5/H6 FAIL): holds for axes actually varied (task_slice / model_family / G) and degenerates for axes not varied (seed / temperature). 'Report the Stack' is correct CONDITIONAL on which stack axes are varied -- the label-vs-stack ratio is a property of the experimental design, not a universal constant.

Sharp F3: V_max dominance is RATE-CONDITIONAL — at low rates (≤2.0%) V_max captures 57-67% of lift (consistent with iter-196 57%); at high rates (≥3.0%) V_max retention climbs to 74-78%, other V-stat features become relatively more important. Sharp F4: 4sensor (no raw) is uniformly WORSE than 20raw at every rate (gap +$0.123 to +$0.210/tx), confirming iter-188's finding that V-stat features ENHANCE the raw block, don't replace it. Operational: deploy V_max alone for low-risk deployments (base rate ≤2.0%); deploy full 4-sensor stack for high-risk deployments (base rate ≥3.0%); never deploy 4sensor without raw.

claim: P7 empirical counterfactual G' on the actual 4-method N2 rollout pool (40 steps x 4 methods x 16 prompts x 8 rollouts = 5120 prompts at G=8, 2560 per-method cells). The empirical useful group utility (GU) at the SAME binary reward pool scales GU@G=8=0.2707 -> GU@G=16=0.5469 -> GU@G=32=0.7844 -> GU@G=64=0.9375 - a 3.46x spread. 159/160 (method,step) cells show empirical GU@G=16 strictly > empirical GU@G=8 (the smallest G' in {16,32,64} that strictly beats G=8 is G'=16 on 159 cells and G'=32 on 1 cell). Per-method uniformity is strong (range 0.018-0.063 at every G' across grpo/aero/gift/areal); grpo mean chosen G = 16.00, aero 16.00, gift 16.40, areal 16.00. Hypotheses (all 4 PASS): H1 PASS (159/160 >= 50% G=16 wins), H2 PASS (saturation match by construction), H3 PASS (160/160 escalate), H4 PASS (median overhead G'-G = 8 <= G'_max - G). This is the FIRST measurement that exploits the empirical structure of the actual rollout pool (instead of iid Beta-Binomial posterior predictive) to construct counterfactual G in {16,32,64} via 2-, 4-, 8-prompt merging of the same G=8 pool. The paper-facing prescription: bump from G=8 to G=16 every step (median overhead = 1x G_BASE). Honest negatives: (i) the G=16 measurement is exact on the paired-prompt pool, not on real G=16 of one prompt, so prompt-conditional iid across rollouts is assumed and anti-herding delta_div in [0.13,0.23] would slightly lower the real GU; (ii) per-prompt counterfactual is still undone - we know which prompts are saturated (k=0 or k=8) but the G=16 budget cannot be assigned to specific prompts without re-rolling.
